display.title: Mesiras Nefesh of a Child, Part 2
display.summary_short: The young Frierdiker Rebbe is freed from jail, the crooked policeman is exposed, and the Rebbe Rashab draws three lessons. Then the end of the discourse Se'u Yedeichem Kodesh.
display.summary_long: In the days after the Frierdiker Rebbe's release in 5687, the storyteller recalls the discourses he said on his return and finishes last week's story, again in the Frierdiker Rebbe's words. In the dark cell, a match from his friend shows that the frightening noises come from a calf tied up with a muzzle. Before he finishes reviewing Mishnayos, the officer who struck him lets him out, apologizing once he learns the boy's uncle is the respected Raza, and begs him to keep the slap a secret. The storyteller pauses for an important lesson: if anyone hurts you or makes you uncomfortable and says not to tell, tell a parent or teacher. At the police chief's office, witnesses defend Reb Dovid, and the hidden calf proves that the policeman and his brother stole it to frame him. The policeman is punished and dismissed. The Rebbe Rashab praises his son and gives three lessons: honor every Jew, stand up for a Jew even at risk, and always know some Torah by heart. The storyteller closes with the end of the discourse Se'u Yedeichem Kodesh, on turning bad traits into good, and its niggun.
display.lesson: Honor every Jew, stand up for another Jew even at a risk, and always carry Torah by heart. If someone hurts you and says to keep it secret, tell a trusted adult.
